statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks judged on the booking page and its submit flow. Served by a static Python http.server fixture (HTTP/1.0, directory listing at /), so server-side behaviour (POST /book, headers) reflects this host, not necessarily a production deployment.

page.framework: none (static HTML + one shared stylesheet, zero scripts)
page.notes: Single evening-class booking form for 'Riverside Training Centre'. 40 DOM elements, 0 scripts, 0 inline handlers, one stylesheet (../base.css, 3 KB) shared by sibling fixture designs. Header nav links to / (a raw directory listing) and /roster (404). The form POSTs to /book, which the host answers with 501. Sibling directories (account-recovery/, catalogue/, contact-lead/, event-registration/) are separate designs, not linked from this page, and out of scope for this run.

a11ytree (computed AX tree + real Tab order)
discoverability (raw vs rendered, crawler screenshot pair)
heap summaries (baseline and after 10x fill/validate interaction)

Form probe: field attributes (email autocomplete=username), no class picker, no :user-invalid rules or live/alert regions, POST /book -> 501, aria-current=page on the '/' link, no meta description/canonical/JSON-LD/OG.
Render under ar-EG / Asia/Tokyo: text identical to default, lang=en, ltr, 0 physical left/right CSS properties.
Attempted capture after a scripted filled submit. INCONCLUSIVE: it shows the empty form, not the post-submit state, so it is not used as evidence. The 501 is evidenced by form-probe.json instead.

findings.summary: The booking form has no way to choose which class you are booking. The lede says 'Pick a class, tell us who is coming', but the form only collects personal details and 'Confirm booking' commits to an unspecified class.
findings.evidence: form-probe: the form's elements are name, email, address, postcode, notes and a submit button; hasClassPicker=false (no select, radio, date or class-named field). The DOM confirms the lede copy 'Pick a class...'. The page shows no class name, date or time anywhere before the commit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a required class choice inside the form, either a native <select name="class" required> or a radio-group <fieldset> of upcoming sessions with their day and time, and show the chosen class back on the 'Confirm booking' step. Use native controls so validation and autofill still work without JS (MWG 'forms').

findings.summary: Submitting the form dead-ends: the action /book answers POST with 501 'Unsupported method' (and GET with 404). The user lands on a raw server error page with no recovery path and no confirmation.
findings.evidence: form-probe POSTed a valid filled form to form.action (/book): status 501 'Unsupported method (POST)', body is the host's generic 'Error response' page. recon: GET /book -> 404. The console logged 'Failed to load resource: 501' for /book. Confidence is medium because the host is a static fixture server, but this is the behaviour a user of this deployment gets.
findings.suggestedFix: Back the form action with a handler that accepts POST, stores the booking and redirects (POST-redirect-GET) to a confirmation page naming the class, date and next steps. On failure, re-render the form with the user's input preserved and an error summary at the top (role=alert) that offers a retry.

findings.summary: The contact email field uses autocomplete="username", a sign-in/sign-up token, on a booking form that has no account or password. Autofill gets the wrong hint: browsers may offer saved login identifiers, or treat the form as a credential form, instead of filling the user's contact email.
findings.evidence: form-probe and dom: <input id="email" type="email" autocomplete="username">. The form has no password field and no sign-in/sign-up purpose. MWG autofill-address-form (the guide for contact/address forms) prescribes autocomplete="email" for email inputs. The 'username for email' advice in autofill-sign-up-form applies only to credential forms. Secondary point: the street address is a single-line <input>, whereas the guide recommends a <textarea autocomplete="street-address"> for varied address formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the email field to <input type="email" id="email" name="email" autocomplete="email" spellcheck="false" required>. Consider making the address a <textarea autocomplete="street-address">. Keep name="name" autocomplete="name" and postcode autocomplete="postal-code", which are already correct.

findings.summary: No dark mode: the page ignores prefers-color-scheme and does not declare color-scheme, so the bright #f4f5f8/#fff surfaces and light form controls stay the same for users who ask for dark.
findings.evidence: screenshot under prefers-color-scheme: dark is byte-identical to the default capture (both 36147 bytes) and visibly light. The features census (complete, 1 sheet): color-scheme 0, light-dark() 0, prefers-color-scheme conditions 0; the only @media is (max-width: 44rem).
findings.suggestedFix: In base.css add :root { color-scheme: light dark; } and define the tokens with light-dark(), e.g. --ink: light-dark(#1b1b1f, #ececf1); --paper: light-dark(#fff, #1c1c22); --wash: light-dark(#f4f5f8, #121216). Then re-check accent/ink contrast in both schemes. Add <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> to avoid a flash (MWG dark-mode). light-dark() is newly available, so ship a plain @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) token override as the fallback.

findings.summary: Error handling relies only on the browser's transient native validation bubble. Invalid fields get no persistent visual state, no inline message and no hint, and no error region is announced.
findings.evidence: form-probe: the empty form fails checkValidity() (4 required fields, each with 'Please fill out this field.'). The stylesheet has 0 :user-invalid/:invalid/aria-invalid rules (features census also shows :user-invalid 0). No field has aria-describedby. No [role=alert] or [aria-live] region exists. Nothing tells users that the fields are required until they submit, and the email has no format hint.
findings.suggestedFix: Follow MWG validate-input-after-interaction: keep the native required/type=email constraints, add input:user-invalid { border-color; background } plus an adjacent .error-msg revealed with input:user-invalid + .error-msg, and link hints and errors with aria-describedby / aria-errormessage. Mark required fields in the label text. :user-invalid is Baseline widely available, so no fallback is mandatory.

findings.summary: The header link 'Evening classes' (href="/") has aria-current="page" while the user is on /booking/, so assistive technology announces the wrong page as current. The bold style tells sighted users the same wrong thing.
findings.evidence: form-probe ariaCurrent: [{href: 'http://127.0.0.1:8765/', cur: 'page'}] while location.href is http://127.0.0.1:8765/booking/. The a11ytree exposes this link with the current-page state, and base.css renders [aria-current=page] at font-weight 600. axe does not flag this (it is a semantic mismatch, not a rule violation).
findings.suggestedFix: Set aria-current="page" only on the link whose href resolves to the current URL. Add a 'Book a class' nav item pointing to /booking/ and mark that one current, or drop aria-current from the '/' link.

findings.summary: The header navigation does not orient or guide users. 'Roster' goes to a 404, and 'Evening classes' goes to a raw server directory listing. Combined with F6, neither nav item helps users understand where they are or where to go next.
findings.evidence: recon fetch: GET /roster -> 404 'File not found'. GET / -> 200 'Directory listing for /' (a list of fixture folders). The console logged a 404 for /roster during the probe. Confidence is medium because the host is a static fixture.
findings.suggestedFix: Point the nav links at real pages: a class listing at the 'Evening classes' URL, and a roster page or remove the link. Include the booking page in the nav with aria-current="page" so users can see where they are.

findings.summary: A form that collects name, email, street address and postcode is served over plain HTTP with no Content-Security-Policy and no X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: https=false; content-security-policy missing; x-content-type-options missing. The navigation entry shows nextHopProtocol http/1.0. The form method=post action=/book is same-origin over http. Confidence is medium: loopback is a secure context and the fixture host may not reflect production, but nothing in the response sets a policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve over HTTPS. Send Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script' (enforced, not report-only), and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The page has no scripts, so a strict policy costs nothing (MWG security).

findings.summary: Reserving a place at an evening class requires a full street address and postcode, with no stated purpose. That is more personal data than the task evidently needs.
findings.evidence: form-probe: address (autocomplete=street-address) and postcode (autocomplete=postal-code) are both required=true. The page copy gives no reason (for example postal materials or catchment eligibility). Otherwise the page is clean: 0 cookies, 0 third-party origins, 0 trackers, 0 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask only for what the booking needs (name and email). If address or postcode is genuinely required, say why next to the field and how long it is kept. Otherwise make those fields optional or remove them (MWG privacy: data minimisation).

findings.summary: No browser-enforced defences are configured: no HSTS, no clickjacking protection (no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options), no Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, referrer-policy and permissions-policy all missing, and there is no CSP to carry frame-ancestors. A framed copy of this PII form could be overlaid (clickjacking).
findings.suggestedFix: Once on HTTPS, send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, CSP frame-ancestors 'self', Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() (MWG security, privacy).

findings.summary: The page has a good descriptive <title> but no meta description, so search and share snippets have to guess.
findings.evidence: form-probe metaDescription=false. discoverability metaDescriptionPresentInRaw=null (absent). The title 'Evening class booking - Riverside Training Centre' is present in the raw HTML.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <meta name="description" content="Book a place on an evening class at Riverside Training Centre, Monday to Thursday 6pm to 9pm.">. Modern Web Guidance has no SEO guide; this is the Lighthouse SEO bar.

findings.summary: The only render-blocking resource (base.css) is served uncompressed with no Cache-Control or validators, over HTTP/1.0, so repeat visits re-download it.
findings.evidence: har-summary hygiene: base.css listed in missingCacheHeaders and uncompressedTextOver2KB (3179 B, content-encoding none). renderBlockingCandidates: base.css (parser-inserted, VeryHigh). Navigation nextHopProtocol http/1.0. The absolute cost is small (5.5 KB total page weight).
findings.suggestedFix: Serve static assets with compression (br/gzip), a versioned filename and Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3. Optionally inline the 3 KB of critical CSS.

findings.summary: body sets font: 16px/1.5, a fixed pixel size that overrides the user's browser and OS default text size. People who raise their default font size get no larger text (page zoom still works).
findings.evidence: dom css: 'body { font: 16px / 1.5 system-ui, ... }'. Headings use rem, so they inherit from the root, but body copy and form controls (font: inherit) stay pinned at 16px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a relative size: body { font: 100%/1.5 system-ui, ... } (or 1rem) so body text and inherited controls scale with the user's text-size preference (MWG respect-os-text-scale).

findings.summary: This multi-page site's navigations (nav to booking, booking to confirmation) swap instantly. There is no cross-document view-transition opt-in.
findings.evidence: features census (complete): @view-transition 0, view-transition-name 0. 0 scripts, so there is no same-document transition either.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } } to base.css. It is a pure progressive enhancement; browsers without support just navigate normally (MWG cross-document-transitions).

checkOutcomes.evidence: 'Confirm booking' commits the user without showing what they are committing to (no class, date, time or price), and there is no cancellation information. The commitment is not visible before confirmation.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR by-resource-type + images inventory via DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 images or decorative assets. Total transfer is 5.5 KB (document 1.8 KB, CSS 3.2 KB).

checkOutcomes.method: Script inventory + HAR over the load window
checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 scripts, 0 timers and 0 background fetches. The HAR shows only the document, the stylesheet and the browser's favicon request.

checkOutcomes.method: trackers + HAR third-party origins + DOM media inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 third-party origins and no web fonts (system stack), video, audio or animation.

checkOutcomes.method: Source/DOM inspection for WebMCP registration and agentic-form affordances
checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 scripts, so no WebMCP tool registration. The form is plain semantic HTML with labelled fields, which agents can already read.
checkOutcomes.reason: Emerging, contextual principle. There is no web-uplift.json intent declaring an agent-facing surface, and a single-venue booking form does not need dedicated agent tools. This is an opportunity, not an obligation: once F1/F2 are fixed, a WebMCP 'book_class' tool or agentic-form annotations would be a cheap add.

checkOutcomes.method: Source/DOM inspection for built-in AI (LanguageModel/Summarizer) usage
checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 scripts. The page has no text-generation, summarisation or classification task.
checkOutcomes.reason: The page has no task that on-device inference would improve. The content is a short form plus two sentences of opening hours.

checkOutcomes.method: heap summary baseline vs after 10x (fill all fields, clear, reportValidity) via --interact
checkOutcomes.evidence: Retained heap 0.97 MB -> 1.22 MB (+250 KB, +3.4k nodes) across 10 cycles. The page has 0 scripts and 0 listeners, so this growth is the injected harness script plus native validation UI, not page-retained state. No Detached* constructor appears in either summary.

checkOutcomes.method: heap summary totals + DOM element count + performance.memory
checkOutcomes.evidence: 40 DOM elements. usedJSHeapSize 1.2 MB, heap self size 0.97 MB (mostly V8/native builtins). Proportionate for a static form.

checkOutcomes.method: Constructor summaries before/after 10x interaction + script/handler inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: No Detached* constructors before or after. The top-25 constructors bottom out at 84 B entries, so any detached-node population would rank. The page registers 0 listeners and 0 timers (0 scripts, 0 inline on* handlers).

principleOutcomes.reason: Emerging, contextual principle with no declared agent-facing intent. The page has no scripts or agent tools, and no task that on-device AI would improve. Recorded as an opportunity (a WebMCP booking tool once the flow works), not penalised.
